newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PEARCE FACES TOUGH FIRST GAME AS FOREST BOSS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PEARCE FACES TOUGH FIRST GAME AS FOREST BOSS.

text.p: Nottingham Forest will need to display all the well-known battling qualities of their new caretaker manager Stuart Pearce to emerge from Saturday's tough battle against Arsenal with anything but another defeat.

Forest are currently rock-bottom in the English premier league after going 16 matches without a win. Manager Frank Clark quit on Thursday, the club are at the centre of takeover talks and, amid it all, Pearce has taken on the task of bringing some much needed stability to a rapidly-sinking ship.

But all is not yet lost and Forest probably have enough quality players and enough time to pull out of their nosedive. They have been desperately unlucky with injuries affecting key players, are badly lacking in confidence and face a tough Christmas programme against Arsenal, Manchester United, local rivals Leicester and a trip to West Ham.
But if anyone can restore some pride and belief in Forest, that man is Pearce who will review his position when the future of the club has finally been decided.

The veteran full-back wants to see how the role will affect his play -- at domestic and international level -- before committing himself to the job if it is offered to him on a permanent basis when the club's new, but as yet unknown, owners take over.

Forest chairman Irving Korn said today: "Stuart Pearce will take on the job as caretaker manager until mid-January. But he wants to see how it would affect his playing career in trying to combine it with doing the manager's job."
He added: "If he feels he can cope with all that is involved then he is going to come and see me after Christmas and we will discuss a proper contract.
"He also wants to see what will happen in terms of any consortiums who may or not be about to take over at the club. We would hope that he would carry on as manager until the end of the season.
"On the playing side Stuart also wants to see how becoming a manager might affect his international career because the fellow does absolutely love playing football.
"But we will have to see what the new owners, whoever they are, think. They will want to talk to Stuart but they might have completely different ideas as to what they want to do."
And Korn revealed when Clark resigned his post he recommended that 34-year-old Pearce should be the man to replace him at the City Ground.
"It was Frank's idea to keep it in the family in terms of appointing Stuart. He felt he was ideal for the job."

Pearce did not attend the news conference called by Forest to announce his appointment because he was out preparing for tomorrow's home clash against Arsenal who start as strong favourites to take all three points and keep up their challenge for the title.

But he needed only a few hours to make his first signing when he secured former Forest favourite Nigel Clough on a temporary loan from Manchester City. He should go straight into the side for Saturday's match.

Arsenal Manager Arsene Wenger will be without suspended captain Tony Adams and French midfielder Patrick Vieira, but top scorer Ian Wright is in superb form and against Forest's shell-shocked defence could well add to the 20 goals he has already scored this season.
